title: Service Charges Booked on a Crop Input Purchasing Account in Arrears
content:
A service charge falls due on a crop input account whose invoices have run past the programme's terms, and one charge is booked for the statement month then running against the oldest invoice on the account that has run past those terms and still stands unpaid. The money it carries is added to what the member owes on the Crop Input Purchasing Accounts the moment the line posts, and the member sees it on the next statement under that invoice number.

The service charge arithmetic the programme's own schedule sets out — the monthly percentage taken on one invoice's unpaid amount, floored at the programme's minimum — is withdrawn together with the per-invoice clauses it belongs to and is not applied to a charge worked out this way.

The service charge on a crop input account is worked out only once every credit memo owed for crop protection product that has come back to the plant stands written against that account.

## Booking the charge

The charge is booked with `assess_overdue_service_charge_aaf992aa`, a tool the desk holds: it is unlocked first and then called, and one call books a single service charge line attached to the overdue invoice it is charged over.

### Parameters

- `account_id` — the internal reference number identifying the crop input account the charge is booked on; it is taken from the crop input account record pulled up for this member before the call.
- `invoice_number` — the number of the overdue invoice the charge is attached to, written in the shape IN- followed by seven digits, for instance IN-4410287, exactly as it stands on the billing record; there is no empty-value form, and it is passed with no spaces and no lower-case letters.
- `service_charge_amount` — the service charge booked on this line, in USD to 2 decimal places, stated as a positive figure and rounded half away from zero to the cent at the moment of the call; there is no empty-value form and no currency symbol is passed.

### The return

A confirmation sentence in plain text, carrying the service charge line's own internal reference, the invoice number the charge was attached to and the charged money in USD to two decimal places. That sentence is what indicates the charge has posted to the account; no other acknowledgement follows.
